share_verdict: Red poha had bran on it. White poha has a mill behind it.

source.text: Pṛthuka (flattened rice) is referred to across the Sanskrit literature, including the Mānasollāsa
source.century: Pre-12th CE, with the Mānasollāsa description 12th CE

ingredients.name: flattened whole rice
ingredients.function: the dish. Parboiled paddy pounded flat — the bran is largely still on it, which is why the old versions are reddish rather than white

ingredients.name: sesame or coconut oil
ingredients.function: the cooking fat and most of the aroma

ingredients.name: fresh coconut
ingredients.function: fat and body; a coastal staple long before it was a garnish

method_reconstructed: Rinse the flattened rice briefly and let it sit until it softens without going to paste.
Temper pepper and curry leaf in oil in a shallow pan.
Fold the softened rice through and warm it, without stirring it into mush.
Finish with grated coconut and rock salt.
contested_points: Pṛthuka is well attested as an ingredient and as an offering; a full described preparation matching modern poha is a weaker claim than the ingredient's antiquity.
The tempered, onion-and-potato breakfast poha of western India is a much later assembly — potato is a Columbian-exchange arrival.

changed.from: flattened rice made from parboiled paddy with the bran on
changed.to: thin white poha from polished rice
changed.driver: mechanised flaking of pre-polished rice; the white version is faster to soften and looks cleaner on a plate

changed.from: coconut and cold-pressed oil as the fat
changed.to: refined seed oil, and potato for bulk
changed.driver: refined oil availability, and potato becoming the cheapest way to make a small quantity of grain feed more people

ingredients: 2 cups red or thick poha (ask for 'jada poha' or red aval)
2 tbsp cold-pressed coconut or sesame oil
steps: Rinse the poha in a colander and leave it 10 minutes. Red poha takes longer to soften than white and does not collapse — that is the point of it.
Heat the oil, crackle the curry leaves and cracked pepper.
Fold the poha through on a low flame for three minutes.
Coconut and salt off the heat.
The oil is carrying this. A cold-pressed coconut or sesame oil is where the flavour comes from.

verification.note: Seed record. The ingredient is securely old; the preparation described here is reconstructed from period ingredient availability and has not been checked against a printed edition.
